card.name: Daychovo horo
card.era: Originated in North Bulgaria; popularized post-WWII
card.tagline: Northern Bulgarian 9/8 circle dance with a calling leader.
card.profile: A Bulgarian folk dance in nine-beat meter (9/16 or 9/8), the Daychovo-type rhythm being 2+2+2+3. Unusual in being a circle dance that nevertheless has a leader who calls figures/variations. Traditionally danced 'na prava' (straight line) by men grasping neighbors' belts in an X, or in an open mixed circle with V handhold. Originating in North Bulgaria, accompanied by gaida, gadulka, kaval, accordion and tapan (English Wikipedia; Folk Dance Federation of California).
card.insight: The name means 'Daycho's dance.' Per dance researcher Boris Conev (via Dick Crum), it traces to a 19th-century Pleven cattle merchant named Daycho whose downfall after 1878 inspired derisive tavern lyrics set to a lively 9/16 melody (Folk Dance Federation of California).
